content.title: Methodology & Aggregation Rules
content.description: Coal/lignite reserves are reported as geological estimates (MT) classified by confidence level. Renewable potential is assessed capacity (MW) based on resource surveys. Regional aggregations are simple sums. SHARE formulas divide at the same grain (state or national) then display as percentage.
assumptions: Renewable potential = technically feasible capacity, not installed
limitations: Single time period — no trend analysis possible
State boundaries as of 2025 Census delimitation
Hydrocarbons data available for producing states only

terms.definition: Million Tonnes — unit for coal, lignite, and crude oil reserves
Megawatt — unit for renewable energy potential (assessed capacity)
Billion Cubic Metres — unit for natural gas reserves
Reserves established with the highest degree of geological confidence under UNFC-2009
Technically feasible energy generation capacity based on resource surveys, not installed capacity

content.description: Significant null values exist in measure columns for states without relevant resources. Coal: 33% null (6 states have no coal deposits). Lignite: 78% null (only 3 states). Crude Oil/Natural Gas: 78% null (only 4 producing states). These are true zeros (no resource) rather than data collection failures.
content.impactScope: States without the relevant resource type show null; excluded from ranking/composition analysis for that resource.
